overview: Rain and mountain snow keep coming in from the Pacific this week. Whistler and the Cascades get the most snow early, while the Northern Rockies see light showers Monday, then drier days before a more active pattern from Thanksgiving onward.

regions.title: Coast Mountains
regions.text: Whistler is the best bet this week, with a total of 32" over the next few days. Its biggest day is Wednesday, with snow mixed with rain and warmer air keeping the snow line high. Expect rain at the base on several days, so the snow will be heaviest at the top of the mountain.

regions.title: Cascades
regions.text: Mt. Baker leads the Cascades with a total of 19", peaking Wednesday, when rain and snow mix together. Crystal Mountain could see its snow rise, with the National Weather Service calling for 13 to 28 inches from Monday through Thursday night. Strong southeast winds and gusts up to 44 mph are expected Monday night into Tuesday.

regions.title: Northern Rockies
regions.text: Jackson Hole's total is 9", with the bulk of the snow coming Thursday and Friday as showers become more likely. Monday brings only a small chance of snow showers, and Tuesday and Wednesday look drier. The atmosphere turns more active ahead of the holiday, with stronger winds Thursday and Friday.

regions.title: Kootenays
regions.text: Snow in the Kootenays is light and mixed with rain, with Whitewater and Revelstoke each forecast at 7". Snow peaks on Thursday, but rain returns Thursday night and Friday, so the snow may not stick at lower elevations.

sources.name: NOAA buoys 51001 / 51101 (method: Powder Buoy, Mike Ruzek)

buoy.text: Buoys 51001 and 51101 near Hawaii popped Nov 11, the swell signal Powder Buoy watches for a Wasatch storm about two weeks later — here Nov 22–28. In past winters a pop raised the chance of a Wasatch storm in that window by roughly 6 to 12 points. Experimental: promising, not proven.
